1-2.word_for_word: gopīnām kāmataḥ kṛṣṇe — from the gopīs' desire directed toward Kṛṣṇa; niḥsīma-prema-saṅgamaḥ — an immeasurable union of love; kātyāyanī-arcana-udbhūta — arising from their worship of Kātyāyanī; tat-prasāda-mahodayaḥ — the great manifestation of her favor; dvā-viṃśe — in the twenty-second chapter; gopa-kanyānām vastra-āharaṇa-līlayā — through the sport of taking the cowherd girls' garments; varam dattvā — having granted the boon; gataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ yajña-śālām — Kṛṣṇa went toward the sacrificial enclosure; prathame māsi mārga-śīrṣe — in the first month, Mārgaśīrṣa
1-2.translation: The gopīs' desire for Kṛṣṇa culminated in an immeasurable union of love, and the great favor they obtained arose from their worship of Kātyāyanī. In the twenty-second chapter, through the pastime of taking the cowherd girls' garments, Kṛṣṇa granted them their boon and then proceeded toward the sacrificial enclosure. ‘In the first month’ means in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.

4.word_for_word: mahā-māye ity-ādi-sambodhanaiḥ — by the vocatives beginning with ‘O Mahāmāyā’; tava na kiñcit aśakyam — nothing is impossible for you; iti sūcayantyaḥ — indicating this; prati-ekam prārthayante — each one prays individually
4.translation: By the forms of address beginning ‘O Mahāmāyā,’ they indicate, ‘Nothing is impossible for you,’ and each of them makes the prayer individually.

5.word_for_word: kṛṣṇa-cetastvam āha — he states that their minds were fixed on Kṛṣṇa; bhūyāt nanda-sutaḥ patiḥ iti — ‘may Nanda's son become our husband’; ānarcuḥ — they worshiped
5.translation: The words ‘they worshiped, praying that Nanda's son might become their husband’ show that their minds were wholly fixed on Kṛṣṇa.

6-7.word_for_word: vratasya pūrva-aṅgam āha — he states the preliminary observance of the vow; uṣasi iti — by the word ‘at dawn’; gotraiḥ nāmabhiḥ — by clan-names, that is, by names; anyonya-ābaddha-bāhavaḥ — their arms linked with one another; parasparam gṛhīta-pāṇayaḥ — holding one another's hands
6-7.translation: He now states the preliminary practice of the vow, beginning with ‘at dawn.’ ‘By their gotras’ means by their names. ‘With arms bound together’ means that they held one another's hands.

8.word_for_word: yogeśvarāṇām īśvaraḥ — the Lord of the masters of yoga; prati-ekam tādṛk-manoratha-pūraṇa-sāmarthyam — the power to fulfill such a desire for each of them individually; darśayati — is indicated; tāsām karmaṇaḥ siddhaye — for the success of their observance; phala-dānāya — in order to give its fruit
8.translation: Calling him ‘the Lord of the masters of yoga’ indicates his power to fulfill the same kind of desire for each girl individually. He came for the success of their observance, in order to award its fruit.

9.word_for_word: nīpam — the nīpa tree; kadambam — the kadamba; bālaiḥ saha — together with the boys
9.translation: ‘Nīpa’ means the kadamba tree. He was there together with the boys.

10.word_for_word: he abalāḥ — O girls; naḥ narma na parihāsaḥ — this statement of mine is not a joke or mockery; yasmāt — because; yūyam vrata-karśitāḥ — you have been made thin by the vow; vrata-śrāntāḥ — exhausted by the observance
10.translation: ‘O girls, what I am saying is not a joke or mere mockery, for you have been made thin and weary by your vow.’

11.word_for_word: tatra — in this matter; asmākam āgrahaḥ — this is our insistence; iti arthaḥ — such is the sense
11.translation: The sense is: ‘This is what we insist upon in the matter.’

12.word_for_word: kṣvelitam — joking, teasing; parihāsam — playful mockery; prema-pariplutāḥ — flooded with love; prema-rasa-nimagnāḥ — immersed in the rasa of love
12.translation: ‘Kṣvelitam’ means playful teasing or mockery. The girls were ‘flooded with love,’ that is, immersed in the rasa of love.

14.word_for_word: tatra mugdhāḥ ūcuḥ — there the innocent younger girls said; aṅga — dear one; bhoḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa — O Śrī Kṛṣṇa; anayam anyāyyam mā kṛthāḥ — do not commit this improper injustice
14.translation: There the innocent girls said, ‘Dear Śrī Kṛṣṇa, do not act unjustly like this.’

15.word_for_word: prauḍhāḥ ūcuḥ — the more mature girls said; no cet — otherwise; rājñe nandāya — to King Nanda; kaṃsāya vā — or to Kaṃsa; bruvāma — we shall tell; he kṛṣṇa — O Kṛṣṇa
15.translation: The more mature girls said, ‘Otherwise, O Kṛṣṇa, we shall tell King Nanda—or even Kaṃsa.’

17.word_for_word: protteruḥ — they came out; nirgatāḥ — they emerged
17.translation: ‘Protteruḥ’ means that they came out of the water.

18.word_for_word: āhatāḥ — affected, struck; īṣat-akṣata-yonīḥ — whose virginity was still intact; vīkṣya — seeing them
18.translation: He saw that, though distressed, their virginity remained intact. This is the sense of the expression glossed here.

19.word_for_word: dhṛta-vratāḥ satyaḥ — though maintaining the vow; vivastrāḥ apaḥ vyagāhata — you entered the water unclothed; apsu snātāḥ — you bathed in the water; etat eva deva-helanam — this itself is disrespect toward the deity; aparādhaḥ eva — indeed an offense; vrata-vaiguṇya-bhītānām — for those afraid that the vow has become defective; prāyaścittam iva āha — he prescribes, as it were, an expiation; asya aṃhasaḥ pāpasya nivṛttaye — for removal of this fault or sin; mūrdhni añjalim baddhvā — placing joined palms at the head; adhaḥ namaḥ praṇāmam kṛtvā — bowing down in obeisance
19.translation: Although you were observing a vow, you entered the water unclothed and bathed there; this itself constitutes disrespect toward the deity, an offense. To those afraid that their vow has thereby become defective, Kṛṣṇa prescribes, as it were, an expiation: for the removal of this fault, place your joined palms upon your head and bow down in obeisance.

20.word_for_word: iti doṣatvena acyutena abhihitam — thus declared by Acyuta to be a fault; vivastra-āplavanam — bathing unclothed; vratasya cyuti-hetum matvā — understanding it as a cause of defect in the vow; tasya pūrti-kāmāḥ — desiring to complete it properly; tam eva nemuḥ — they bowed to him alone; tad-aśeṣa-karmaṇām sākṣāt-kṛtam phala-bhūtam — he who was the manifest fruit of that vow and of all their acts; sa eva avadya-mṛk — he alone removes fault; pāpa-mārjakaḥ — cleanser of sin
20.translation: Acyuta had described bathing unclothed as a fault and a cause of imperfection in the vow. Therefore, wishing to bring the vow to proper completion, they bowed to him alone—the very manifest fruit of that vow and of all their actions. He himself is the remover of fault and the cleanser of sin.

22.word_for_word: dṛḍham atyartham pralabdhāḥ vañcitāḥ — thoroughly deceived and teased; yūyam vivastrāḥ ity-ādinā — by such words as ‘you are naked’; trapayā hāpitāḥ tyājitāḥ — made to give up their reserve through embarrassment; atra āgatya sva-vāsāṃsi iti āgraheṇa — by insisting ‘come here and take your garments’; prastobhitāḥ upahasitāḥ — mocked and laughed at; satyam bravāṇi no narma ity-ādinā — with words such as ‘I speak the truth; this is no joke’; krīḍanavat kāritāḥ — made into objects of play; baddhāñjalim ity-ādi-prāyaścitta-chalena — under the pretext of expiation beginning ‘with joined palms’; tāḥ na abhyasūyan — they did not resent him; doṣa-dṛṣṭyā na apaśyan — they did not look upon him as blameworthy
22.translation: They had been thoroughly teased and deceived by words such as ‘you are naked’; they were made, through embarrassment, to relinquish their reserve by his insistence, ‘come here and take your garments’; they were mocked by such words as ‘I speak the truth, this is no joke’; and, under the pretext of the expiation beginning ‘with joined palms,’ they were made participants in his play. Yet they did not resent him or regard him as blameworthy.

23.word_for_word: preṣṭha-saṅgamena sajjitāḥ vaśī-kṛtāḥ — captivated and brought under control by union with the beloved; gṛhīta-cittāḥ — their minds seized; satyaḥ no celuḥ — they did not move away; tasmin kṛṣṇe lajjāyita-īkṣaṇāḥ — their glances bashfully resting on Kṛṣṇa; lajjā-vilasitam īkṣaṇam yāsām — whose looks displayed bashfulness
23.translation: Captivated by contact with their beloved and with their minds seized by him, they did not move away. Their ‘bashful eyes’ means that their glances toward Kṛṣṇa themselves displayed their modesty.

24.word_for_word: dāmodara iti — by the name Dāmodara; bhakta-vātsalyam darśayati — his tenderness toward devotees is shown; abalāḥ prati — toward the girls
24.translation: The name ‘Dāmodara’ here indicates his tender affection toward his devotees, specifically toward these girls.

25.word_for_word: bhoḥ sādhvyaḥ — O virtuous girls; bhavatīnām mad-arcanam — your worship of me; saṅkalpaḥ manorathaḥ — your resolve and cherished desire; lajjayā akathitaḥ api — though left unspoken out of modesty; mayā viditaḥ — is known by me; saḥ mayā anumoditaḥ — it is approved by me; ataḥ satyaḥ bhavitum arhati — therefore it is fit to come true; arhati iti sambhāvanā-mātra-uktyā — by the merely potential expression ‘is fit’; ātyantikaḥ na bhaviṣyati iti sūcitam — it is indicated that the fulfillment will not be immediate or final at this moment
25.translation: ‘O virtuous girls, I know the resolve and cherished desire underlying your worship of me, even though out of modesty you did not speak it. I approve that desire; therefore it is fit to become true.’ By phrasing this only as a possibility—‘it is fit to become true’—he indicates that its complete fulfillment will not occur immediately at that moment.

26.word_for_word: tat kutaḥ — why is that; na mayi iti — he answers with the words ‘in me’; kāmāya punaḥ kāma-bhogāya — for lust, that is, for renewed sensual enjoyment; viṣaya-mahimnā — by the greatness of the object; kāmasya api śānti-hetutvāt — because even desire becomes pacified; kāma-aprarohe dṛṣṭāntaḥ — an example for desire not sprouting again; bharjitā dagdhā kvathitā pakvā dhānā yava-ādi — parched, burned or cooked grains such as barley; bījāya aṅkura-udgamāya na — are no longer fit as seed for sprouting; prāya iti — the word ‘generally’; sva-icchayā punaḥ praroham api sūcayati — leaves open sprouting again by the Lord's own will; dhruva-ādīnām tathā darśanāt — as seen in cases such as Dhruva
26.translation: Why will ordinary sensual desire not arise from this? Kṛṣṇa answers with ‘desire directed toward me.’ Because of the greatness of its object, even desire becomes a cause of the cessation of ordinary desire. He gives the example of grain such as barley that has been parched, burned or cooked: it no longer functions as seed capable of sprouting. The qualification ‘generally’ nevertheless leaves room for desire to arise again by the Lord's own will, as is seen in the cases of Dhruva and others.

27.word_for_word: siddhāḥ — successful; pūrṇa-manorathāḥ — their desires fulfilled; imā āgāminī rātrīḥ mayā raṃsyatha — ‘during these coming nights you shall sport with me’; āryā — the venerable goddess; kātyāyanī — Kātyāyanī; satīḥ — the virtuous girls
27.translation: They became successful, their cherished desire assured of fulfillment. This is expressed in Kṛṣṇa's words, ‘During these coming nights you shall sport with me.’ ‘Āryā’ refers to the venerable goddess Kātyāyanī, and ‘satīḥ’ means the virtuous girls.

28.word_for_word: bhaktyā anukampya kanyāḥ tāḥ — having compassionately favored those girls because of their devotion; tad-vivarjita-yajvanām — of the sacrificers who were devoid of that devotion; patnī-anugrahataḥ — by bestowing favor upon their wives; teṣām karma-mahā-madam ahan — he struck down their great pride in ritual action
28.translation: Having compassionately favored those girls because of their devotion, Kṛṣṇa next favored the wives of sacrificers who themselves lacked such devotion, and thereby broke the sacrificers' great pride in ritual action.

29.word_for_word: atha tāsām gamana-anantaram — then, after those girls had departed; yajña-patnīṣu prasādam vaktum ārabhate — the narration begins to describe grace toward the sacrificers' wives; līlā-antara-ārambhe — at the beginning of another pastime; saḥ nidāgha-samayaḥ eva — it should be understood as a time of heat; sahāgrajaḥ — together with his elder brother Baladeva; vastra-āharaṇa-dine tat-sāhitya-abhāvāt — because Baladeva was absent on the day of the garment-taking pastime; gopaiḥ parivṛtaḥ — surrounded by cowherds; teṣām apekṣā-viśeṣāt — because those cowherds are especially needed in the coming pastime; vṛndāvanāt gataḥ dūram — having gone some distance from Vṛndāvana; kāmyaka-vanam gataḥ — he first went to Kāmyaka forest; paścāt yamunām āgataḥ — afterward he came to the Yamunā; dhenu-jala-pāyanārtham — to give water to the thirsty cows; madhyāhnam — at midday; yajña-patnīṣu anna-prārthanā-rūpa-kṛpārtham — for the mercy that would take the form of requesting food from the sacrificers' wives
29.translation: After the girls departed, the narration begins another pastime, one that will describe Kṛṣṇa's grace toward the sacrificers' wives. This episode is to be understood as occurring during a period of heat. Hence Kṛṣṇa is now said to be with his elder brother Baladeva, who had not been present during the garment-taking pastime, and he is surrounded by cowherd boys because they have a special role in what follows. Having gone some distance from Vṛndāvana, he first entered the Kāmyaka forest; later, to water the cows when thirst arose from the heat, he came southward toward the Yamunā. His reaching there at midday, when the boys had not eaten, provides the occasion for his mercy toward the sacrificers' wives in the form of a request for food.

30.word_for_word: nidāghaḥ uṣṇa-upagamaḥ — nidāgha can mean the coming of heat; nidāghaḥ grīṣma-ṛtuḥ — it ordinarily means summer; tat-svīkāre he-mante prathame māsi iti upakramaḥ virudhyeta — if that sense were accepted it would conflict with the earlier statement that this was the first month of winter; ataḥ atra nidāgha-padena sveda-ambu jñeyam — therefore here nidāgha is to be understood as sweat-water or heat; nidāghaḥ sveda-ambu — nidāgha may mean perspiration; tat-karaḥ arkaḥ nidāgha-arkaḥ — the sun that produces it is ‘nidāghārka’; madhya-pada-lopī samāsaḥ — the compound has an omitted middle member; tasya ātāpaḥ — its heat; tīvre madhyāhne sati — when midday was intense; drūmān vīkṣya iti anvayaḥ — the construction continues with ‘seeing the trees’; ātapatram iva ācaranti — acting like parasols; ātapatrāyitāḥ — having become parasol-like; vrajaukasaḥ — ‘residents of Vraja’ qualifies the trees; ātmanaḥ iti upalakṣaṇam — ‘for himself’ includes for himself and his companions
30.translation: Although ‘nidāgha’ commonly denotes the summer season, taking it that way here would conflict with the chapter's opening statement that the event began in the first month of winter. Here, therefore, the word is understood in the related sense of heat or perspiration. The ‘nidāgha-sun’ is the sun that produces such heat; the compound is explained as one with an omitted middle member. Thus the construction is: when the midday heat had become intense, Kṛṣṇa saw the trees. They had become, as it were, parasols. ‘Residents of Vraja’ qualifies those trees, and ‘for himself’ is inclusive: they gave shelter to him and to his companions.

31.word_for_word: sambuddhy-ātmaka-padyam — the verse consists of vocatives; he stoka-kṛṣṇa — O Stoka-kṛṣṇa; alpaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ yasya — ‘one whose Kṛṣṇa is small,’ an etymological gloss; sarveṣām sambodhanānām paśyata iti kriyā-padena sambandhaḥ — all the vocatives connect with the verb ‘look’; gopa-gaṇanā-kramaḥ — the order in which the cowherds are enumerated; yathā-dṛṣṭi-prāptam — follows the order in which they came into view; ete daśa — these ten; śrī-kṛṣṇasya daśa-dikṣu rakṣaṇārtham — for protecting Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the ten directions; iti kecit sambhāvayanti — some suggest this because they are ten in number; stoka-kṛṣṇa-ādayaḥ aṣṭau — the eight beginning with Stoka-kṛṣṇa; aṣṭa-dikṣu — in the eight directions; devaprastha-varūthau — Devaprastha and Varūtha; ūrdhva-adho-deśayoḥ — above and below; bhadrasenaḥ — Bhadrasena; gopa-sena-adhyakṣaḥ — commander of the cowherd band; rāmaḥ — Balarāma; sarva-apekṣakaḥ — supervisor of all; dūre sthitaḥ — was then at some distance
31.translation: This verse is made up of forms of address: ‘O Stoka-kṛṣṇa,’ and so forth. All the vocatives are governed by the following verb ‘look.’ The order in which the cowherd boys are named is simply the order in which they came into view. Because ten are named, some suggest that they lovingly guarded Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the ten directions: the eight beginning with Stoka-kṛṣṇa in the eight horizontal directions, Devaprastha and Varūtha attending above and below through such services as holding the parasol and clearing the path. Bhadrasena, counted as an eleventh, was commander of the cowherd group. Rāma, who supervised them all, appears to have been standing some distance away at that moment.

32.word_for_word: vipra-bhāryā-anugrahāya yajña-vāṭam gacchan — while going toward the sacrificial enclosure to favor the brāhmaṇas' wives; viprāṇām kāṭhinyam abhipretya — having in mind the hardness of the brāhmaṇas; tebhyaḥ api drumāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ — he praises the trees as superior even to them; caturbhiḥ — in four verses; parārtham eva ekāntena jīvitam yeṣām — whose entire life is exclusively for the sake of others; vāta-varṣa-ādīn svayam sahantaḥ — themselves enduring wind, rain and the like; asmākam vārayanti — they ward these from us
32.translation: As he went toward the sacrificial enclosure to favor the brāhmaṇas' wives, Kṛṣṇa had in mind the hardness of the brāhmaṇas themselves. Therefore, in four verses beginning ‘look,’ he praises the trees as superior even to them: ‘See these trees, whose entire life is wholly devoted to others. They themselves endure wind, rain and the rest while shielding us from them.’

33.word_for_word: sujanasya kṛpāloḥ — of a compassionate good person; arthinaḥ iva — like a supplicant approaching him
33.translation: The comparison is with a needy petitioner approaching a compassionate and noble person.

34.word_for_word: niryāsaḥ — exuded sap; ghana-rasaḥ — thick juice or resin; tokmāḥ — new shoots; pallava-ādi-aṅkurāḥ — sprouts such as tender leaves
34.translation: ‘Niryāsa’ means thick exuded sap or resin, and ‘tokmāḥ’ means new sprouts such as tender leaves.

36.word_for_word: iti abhinandan — praising them in this way; pravāla-ādi-samūhaiḥ nata-śākhānām — whose branches bowed beneath masses of new shoots and the like; tarūṇām madhyena — through the midst of the trees; yamunām prāptaḥ — he reached the Yamunā
36.translation: Praising the trees in this way, Kṛṣṇa passed among them, their branches bowed beneath clusters of new shoots and other growth, and reached the Yamunā.

38.word_for_word: kumārikābhyaḥ pūrvam eva — even earlier, before leaving the girls; tat-narma-ākulatayā — because he was absorbed in that playful joking; agṛhīta-bhojyānām eva nirgāmāt — since they had left without taking food; kṣudhārtāḥ iti uktam — therefore they are described as afflicted by hunger
38.translation: The boys are called hungry because, even earlier, they had gone out without taking food, Kṛṣṇa having been absorbed in his playful joking with the girls.
